newsitem.title: DENMARK: UBS may cut Carlsberg forecasts.
newsitem.headline: UBS may cut Carlsberg forecasts.

text.p: Union Bank of Switzerland on Wednesday said it might cut its year profit forecasts for Carlsberg but would probably maintain its hold recommendation on the Danish brewery group.
Carlsberg reported on Tuesday a rise in first half 1996/97 pre-tax profits but a barely changed operating result.

"The operating result was a little disappointing and the company predicts a whole year 1996/97 result similar to the previous year, so I will probably have to lower my estimates, " a UBS London analyst told Reuters.
UBS earlier forecast a full year pre-tax profit for Carlsberg of 1.685 billion crowns, with the net result at 1.127 billion crowns.
Carlsberg posted a 1995/96 pre-tax profit of 1.570 billion crowns, with net profit at 1.063 billion crowns.
"Carlsberg is normally very careful with its forecasts, so maybe we will downwardly adjust the expected 1996/97 net profit to 1.100 billion crowns," he said.
Carlsberg's report for the six months to March 31, 1997 showed pre-tax profit up to 870 million crowns from 741 million the year before and turnover up to 9.21 billion crowns from 8.54 billion.
Analysts had on average forecast pre-tax profit of 812 million crowns and turnover of 8.99 billion.
But the operating result was 532 million crowns, compared with 530 million in the same period last year and an average forecast of 606 million.
"We will most probably maintain our hold recommendation, but there are at present a lot of uncertain factors about the Carlsberg," the UBS analyst said.

"It is difficult to be positive about the Carlsberg shares until we know the outcome of the Bass and Coca Cola deals. If they both go through, we will seriously consider raising our recommendation," he said.

Carlsberg bottles and distributes Coca Cola products in Denmark and is seeking approval from European Union authorities to extend the alliance to Sweden, and eventually throughout the Nordic and Baltic region, in a jointly-owned company named Coca-Cola Nordic Beverages.

In Britain there is uncertainty about the sale of Carlsberg-Tetley to Bass. Bass seeks to buy Carlsberg's half of the British-based joint venture, thereby becoming Britain's largest brewer but is awaiting clearance from U.K. regulators.
Carlsberg's share traded 11 crowns down at 377 at 0945 GMT on Wednesday. -Joern Nurkka, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33969655
